A.text: Use when asked to review, check or assess a pull request, branch, diff or set of commits, or what a change could break. Run `reposcout review-context . --base <base> --head <head> --profile safe --brief` instead of `git diff`: one call returns the changed hunks, changed definitions, importers, call sites and docs that name them. Also for repo orientation, symbol lookup, change impact and code health.
A.note: Short trigger-first form that names the competing diff command.

B.text: Use when the user asks to review a PR, branch, diff or commits, check changes before merge, find what a change could break, or understand an unfamiliar repository. Before running `git diff` or grepping for callers, run `reposcout review-context . --base <base> --head <head> --profile safe --brief`: it prints the diff hunks, changed definitions, direct importers, call sites and docs naming changed identifiers in one compact output. Other RepoScout commands: orientation and file or symbol reads, dependency and change-impact queries, code-health and duplication reports.
B.note: Quoted trigger phrases, an ordering cue before the diff command and the token figure.

C.text: Use for any code review or change-risk question (review this PR, check this branch before merge, what could these commits break, is this refactor safe) and for exploring an unfamiliar repository (where is X defined, who calls Y, what depends on this file, what is risky or unhealthy here). Start review work with `reposcout review-context . --base <base> --head <head> --profile safe --brief` (diff hunks plus changed definitions, importers, call sites and docs in one compact output) before git diff or grep. Otherwise run `reposcout --help` to pick orientation, symbol, impact or health queries.
C.note: Enumerated situations and question-style phrasings, with the review command and a help fallback.

D.text: Use for any question about a change between two commits, branches or a pull request: reviewing it, judging whether it is safe to merge or ship, explaining what changed, or finding defects, regressions and risks. Run `reposcout review-context . --base <base> --head <head> --profile safe --brief` before `git diff` or `git log`: one call returns the changed hunks, changed definitions, importers, call sites and docs that name them. Also for repo orientation, symbol lookup, change impact and code health.
D.note: Task categories instead of trigger verbs, naming both competing git commands.

E.text: Scout and query software repositories with the RepoScout CLI. Use before exploring an unfamiliar codebase, planning implementation or refactoring work, or selecting files for an agent context; to locate symbols and read known definitions; to map dependencies and change impact; and to measure complexity, duplication, churn, risk and test presence. Also use for any question about a code change, staged, uncommitted, or between two commits, branches or a pull request: reviewing it, judging whether it is safe to merge or ship, explaining what changed, or finding defects, regressions and risks. For committed changes, run `reposcout review-context . --base <base> --head <head> --profile safe --brief` before `git diff` or `git log`: one call returns the changed hunks, changed definitions, importers, call sites and docs that name them.
E.note: General scouting, planning, lookup, impact and health uses first, then D's review categories and command.
